purpose: Establish, by observation, what the four places that declare fleet network state actually say, and where they contradict each other. Exists because tranches T4.1 through T5 migrated the repository's plane vocabulary to canonical names without checking that the repository registry, the runtime registry, or the resolver were reading it. The migration was therefore applied to the repo and not to the fleet: it removed one divergence and created a fourth form of truth. Nothing in the build or test loop compares these four sources, so the divergence is structurally invisible.

sources: S1 infra/registry.json — the repository registry, migrated in T4.3
S2 /etc/cynic/registry.json — the registry the running node loads, read over SSH on the builder
S3 the resolver — /etc/hosts and the dnsmasq instance at 10.10.10.1, queried with dig and getent
S4 the repository code — the plane vocabulary and the DNS zone authority in cynic-protocol and cynic-network
not_verified: the four other fleet nodes could not be reached: 10.10.10.100 timed out on SSH, 10.10.10.101 refused the key. Every observation below comes from the builder alone.
no diff of dnsmasq's own configuration was read; the local entries it serves are inferred from its answers

S1_repository_registry.assessment: canonical vocabulary, and the mesh CIDR satisfies RFC-NET-001 section 6.2. This file is the only one of the four that follows the ratified specification.

S2_runtime_registry.assessment: entirely legacy vocabulary. Its mesh CIDR is 10.20.0.0/24, an RFC 1918 range, which RFC-NET-001 section 6.2 forbids for the overlay. This is the file the node actually loads, so the canonical vocabulary currently governs nothing at runtime.

S3_resolver.zone_served: synapse.cynic — SOA is not served for any zone, and no NS record exists for any of them
S3_resolver.local_resolution: the builder's /etc/hosts already carries kernel, forgejo, surrealdb, builder and proxmox under synapse.cynic
S3_resolver.forwarding: external names resolve (google.com returns 172.217.16.238), so dnsmasq forwards upstream
S3_resolver.service_cynic: no name under service.cynic resolves, on the builder or through dnsmasq
S3_resolver.assessment: the zone is not published, it is answered from local entries on each host. This is not a DNS zone; it is a per-host hosts file with a zone-shaped name.

S4_code.duplicates: crates/cynic-node/src/dns_contract.rs:37 and crates/cynic-inference/src/application/chat_endpoint.rs:56 each hold their own DEFAULT_DNS_ZONE = synapse.cynic
S4_code.assessment: the canonical value exists twice at the correct layers and is overridden twice at higher layers. Nothing imports the L0 authority.

contradictions.statement: The repository registry declares service.cynic and the runtime registry declares synapse.cynic, for the same six nodes at the same addresses.
contradictions.consequence: a node loading S2 produces DNS bundles naming synapse.cynic while the repository expects service.cynic. Nothing reports this because the DTO serde aliases accept both vocabularies and the tests read inline fixtures.

contradictions.statement: service.cynic resolves nowhere. The repository's canonical zone has no published record and no local entry on any observable host.
contradictions.consequence: T4.3 wrote six DNS reservations in service.cynic. None of them is reachable. The migration moved the divergence rather than removing it.

contradictions.statement: The mesh CIDR differs: 100.64.0.0/10 in the repository, 10.20.0.0/24 in the runtime. The runtime value is an RFC 1918 range, which the specification forbids for the overlay because it collides with LANs.
contradictions.consequence: the immunity claimed in RFC-NET-001 section 6.2 does not exist on any running node.

contradictions.statement: Two repository nodes do not exist: cynic-lxc-headscale (10.10.10.40) resolves nowhere, no headscale process listens, and it is absent from the runtime registry. local-builder carries no address at all while 10.10.10.119 is the running builder the runtime calls cynic-builder.
contradictions.consequence: the repository declares fleet members that have never been deployed. A convergence loop iterating the repository registry would plan work for a coordinator that does not exist.

contradictions.statement: The code's authority says service.cynic; the resolver answers synapse.cynic. The runtime seed in cynic-protocol requests a detached signature from https://artifacts.synapse.cynic, which resolves nowhere under either zone.
contradictions.consequence: artifacts.synapse.cynic is an invented endpoint with no executor. The real publication path is HttpArtifactPublisher against provider_control.endpoint, https://pve.synapse.cynic:8006.

contradictions.statement: cynic-core/src/fleet_mesh.rs:206 uses a fifth zone, cynic.ts, which appears nowhere else in the repository.
contradictions.consequence: an orphaned name with no declared meaning.

what_agrees: The six shared nodes carry identical service addresses in S1 and S2. The repository migration did not invent or move any address.
Both registries declare six reservations, and the runtime reservations all point at names that exist in /etc/hosts.
The service CIDR 10.10.10.0/24 and the admin CIDR 192.168.100.0/24 are identical in S1 and S2; only the vocabulary and the mesh CIDR differ.

diagnosis.statement: The divergence is not a vocabulary problem. It is a missing authority: four places declare fleet network state, no two agree, and no mechanism compares them.
why_it_survived: the DTO serde aliases accept both vocabularies, so a canonical registry read by a legacy consumer still parses
every consumer test uses an inline fixture carrying legacy keys, so the suite cannot observe a migrated registry
the resolver answers from per-host files rather than a published zone, so nothing has a single point at which a change would take effect
the repository registry is not the one the node loads, and no test asserts that it should be
diagnosis.consequence_for_the_tranche_sequence: Tranches T4.3 through T5 are prerequisites that are now in place but inert: the canonical vocabulary governs the repository and nothing else. Continuing T6 (86 DAG files) and T6b (2 I/O sites) is independent of this and safe. But no further DNS tranche will converge until one source is declared authoritative and the others are derived from it.

open_decisions.question: Which source is authoritative for the fleet: the repository registry or the runtime registry?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: it determines which file the other three are corrected towards, and therefore the direction of every remaining DNS change
open_decisions.current_evidence: AGENTS.md ranks infra/registry.json as a registry to read and never hardcode; foundation.json ranks observed runtime state above the repository. The two authorities disagree about which one wins.

open_decisions.question: Should service.cynic be published as a real zone, or should the canonical name change to match the zone that is actually served?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: publishing a zone is an infrastructure operation with a certificate implication; renaming the canonical vocabulary back to synapse would discard T4.1 through T4.5
open_decisions.current_evidence: synapse.cynic is not a published zone either — it is answered from /etc/hosts on each host. So neither name has a DNS authority today, and the question is whether to create one.

open_decisions.question: Are cynic-lxc-headscale and local-builder declared-but-absent nodes a deployment debt or registry debt?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: if they are debt, the repository registry overstates the fleet and a convergence loop would plan unreachable work

verification.S3: ssh cynic-builder-ssh 'dig +short @10.10.10.1 forgejo.synapse.cynic A; dig +short @10.10.10.1 forgejo.service.cynic A; grep synapse /etc/hosts'
verification.phantom_nodes: ssh cynic-builder-ssh 'getent hosts cynic-lxc-headscale.synapse.cynic; ss -tlnp | grep 8080'

ratification.promotion_condition: the operator answers D1 and D2. Until then this is a measurement record, not an authority.
ratification.authority_note: infra/ is not a source of truth. The three open decisions are governance acts; this document only states what was observed.
